name: code-writer-worktree-only-writes
body:
Code-writer agents — the core `implementer`, every `*-implementer`, every `test-implementer` generated by the `agent-builder` — must be able to write ONLY inside the project worktree they operate in (`<main>/apg/.worktrees/<project>/`), never the main checkout. Reading main stays allowed.

Today they can write main (verified): `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md`'s "Worktree mirroring (MANDATORY)" bullet (~lines 155-162) and rule 10 "Worktree-mirrored edit grants" (~lines 325-338) mandate that every edit glob be granted at the repo ROOT and mirrored under `apg/.worktrees/*/`, and never say to deny the root. opencode resolves edit globs against the session workspace root (the main checkout), so the root allow (e.g. `"src/*.rs": allow`, `"opencode-suite/**": allow` in the generated `.opencode/agents/implementer.md`) makes main writable. Separately, the fs tools (`apg_rm`/`apg_mv`/`apg_cp`) take that same `permission.edit` allow set as their per-path scope (`ts.apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.agentFsGlobs`) but resolve the candidate against the caller-supplied `directory` (`ts.apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.fsScopeDecision`): with directory = worktree and a repo-relative path it is the ROOT glob that matches, and with directory = main a main path is "in boundary" — main is not structurally refused.

Required:
- The agent-builder template's grant rules become ROLE-AWARE: a code-writer's write grants (edit globs and the fs-tool path scope) are granted ONLY under `apg/.worktrees/*/`; the corresponding repo-root paths are NOT granted (deny-by-default leaves them denied; an explicit root deny is acceptable). Existing mirrored denies stay mirrored. The agent-builder itself keeps its main `.opencode/agents/**` grant, and the optional `release-agent` keeps its per-repo main release-artefact grants (it operates on main and needs no worktree mirror) — see `global.constraint.worktree-isolation`.
- The fs tools decide scope in ONE consistent frame: the granted globs and the candidate path are resolved against the same root, so a worktree-rooted grant matches exactly the worktree path it names; and a candidate path that resolves into the main checkout (outside every project worktree) is REFUSED for a code-writer regardless of the caller-supplied `directory`. The mechanism is a plan decision (see the decision note on this requirement).

Acceptance criteria:
- `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` states that code-writer write grants are worktree-only (`apg/.worktrees/*/<glob>`), that root paths are not granted to code-writers, and that the agent-builder and release-agent are the only generated/suite roles with main write grants; the "Worktree mirroring" bullet and rule 10 no longer instruct a root+mirror pair for code-writers.
- An `apg_rm`/`apg_mv`/`apg_cp` call by a code-writer whose (source or destination) path resolves into the main checkout is refused, whatever `directory` the caller passes; the same op on the matching worktree path inside the granted scope succeeds; a `..`/absolute escape stays refused.
- The opt-in suite e2e (`opencode-suite/tests/boundary.e2e.test.ts`) pins the main-refusal and the worktree-success cases.
- Scope is product source only: `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md`, `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts` (+ the tool files only if the fix needs them), `opencode-suite/tests/boundary.e2e.test.ts`, and `AGENTS.md`. The repo's own `.opencode/agents/**` are consumer artifacts and are NOT edited here. They are regenerated later, AFTER THIS CHANGE IS RELEASED: release a binary that contains the corrected template (it is product source embedded via `include_str!`) → install that released binary → re-run `apg init` (which installs the template into `~/.opencode/agents/`) → restart opencode → dispatch the agent-builder on main. No binary mutation-surface change.
